title: Taiwan's Candidates Hand Out Gifts Before Local Elections
summaryZh: 11月28日地方選舉前，各地候選人推出小物與周邊爭取選民。
summaryHi: 28 नवंबर के स्थानीय चुनाव से पहले ताइवान के उम्मीदवार मतदाताओं को उपहार और सामान दे रहे हैं।
summaryEs: Antes de las elecciones locales del 28 de noviembre, los candidatos en Taiwán reparten regalos y productos.
summaryJa: 11月28日の地方選を前に、台湾の候補者がグッズや小物で有権者にアピール。
summaryKo: 11월 28일 지방선거를 앞두고 대만 후보들이 굿즈와 선물로 유권자 공략.
summaryEn: Before the November 28 local elections, Taiwan's candidates are using gifts and goods to win voters.
paragraphs: As Taiwan heads towards local elections on November 28, candidates for mayor and county magistrate are turning to an old campaign tool: merchandise. From tote bags to teddy bears, the goods are designed to raise funds and keep names in voters' minds.

In Taipei, incumbent mayor Chiang Wan-an of the KMT is selling caps, water bottles, T-shirts and phone wallets, items his team describes as practical for daily life. His range even includes NFC keychains that, when tapped against a compatible phone, lead users to the campaign's theme song.

His challenger, Puma Shen of the DPP, offers T-shirts, embroidered patches and plush versions of the campaign mascots. A spokesperson said the items reflect the slogan "Future Soon" and thanked supporters known as "Ocean Current", a pun on Shen's Chinese name, who have produced their own posters and badges.

Changhua County's race shows a more homely approach. KMT candidate Wei Ping-cheng distributes tissues and wet wipes made at his family's factory, with packets featuring a cartoon portrait drawn by his daughter. Independent Chiu Chien-fu gives out socks, which he says symbolise his determination to walk further with supporters.
In Tainan, where the heat is intense, the KMT's Hsieh Lung-chieh hands out fans printed with his policy pledges, while the DPP's Chen Ting-fei sells teddy bears carrying the message "Tainan is home".
Taiwan will have local elections on November 28. People will choose city mayors and county leaders.
Many candidates are giving small gifts to voters. They hope people will remember their names.
In Taipei, Mayor Chiang Wan-an sells bags, caps, water bottles and T-shirts. One key ring can send a phone to his campaign song. His rival, Puma Shen, has T-shirts, towels and soft toys.
In Changhua County, one candidate gives tissues with a cartoon of his face. His daughter drew it. Another candidate gives socks. He says he walks a lot and wants to go far with his supporters.
In Tainan, which is very hot, one candidate gives hand fans. Another sells teddy bears with the words "Tainan is home".
With Taiwan's local elections coming on November 28, candidates for mayor and county magistrate are trying a friendly way to win support: free gifts and campaign goods.

In Taipei, Mayor Chiang Wan-an of the KMT, who wants a second term, is selling bags, caps, water bottles, T-shirts and phone wallets to raise money. His team says they chose useful everyday items. A special keychain can send a signal to a phone and open the campaign's song.

His DPP rival, Puma Shen, offers T-shirts, towels and soft toys of the campaign mascots. His team also thanked fans who call themselves "Ocean Current", a joke on Shen's Chinese name, for making their own posters and stickers.

In Changhua County, candidates are giving out tissues, sponges, wet wipes and face masks. KMT candidate Wei Ping-cheng's tissue packets show a cartoon of him drawn by his daughter. Independent Chiu Chien-fu hands out socks, saying he walks long distances and wants to go further with his supporters.
In hot Tainan, KMT candidate Hsieh Lung-chieh offers hand fans printed with his main promises, while the DPP's Chen Ting-fei sells teddy bears carrying her message, "Tainan is home".

As Taiwan heads towards local elections on November 28, candidates for mayor and county magistrate are turning to an old campaign tool: merchandise. From tote bags to teddy bears, the goods are designed to raise funds and keep names in voters' minds.

In Taipei, incumbent mayor Chiang Wan-an of the KMT is selling caps, water bottles, T-shirts and phone wallets, items his team describes as practical for daily life. His range even includes NFC keychains that, when tapped against a compatible phone, lead users to the campaign's theme song.

His challenger, Puma Shen of the DPP, offers T-shirts, embroidered patches and plush versions of the campaign mascots. A spokesperson said the items reflect the slogan "Future Soon" and thanked supporters known as "Ocean Current", a pun on Shen's Chinese name, who have produced their own posters and badges.

Changhua County's race shows a more homely approach. KMT candidate Wei Ping-cheng distributes tissues and wet wipes made at his family's factory, with packets featuring a cartoon portrait drawn by his daughter. Independent Chiu Chien-fu gives out socks, which he says symbolise his determination to walk further with supporters.
In Tainan, where the heat is intense, the KMT's Hsieh Lung-chieh hands out fans printed with his policy pledges, while the DPP's Chen Ting-fei sells teddy bears carrying the message "Tainan is home".

With Taiwan's local elections set for November 28, mayoral and county magistrate hopefuls are leaning heavily on a time-honoured campaign tactic: branded giveaways. The merchandise serves a dual purpose, raising funds while keeping candidates' names firmly in the public eye.

In Taipei, KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an, who is seeking re-election, has assembled a range of tote bags, caps, insulated bottles and leather phone wallets, which his campaign insists were chosen for their everyday practicality. The most novel item is an NFC keychain that, once tapped against a compatible phone, directs users to his campaign anthem.

His DPP challenger, Puma Shen, is offering embroidered patches, towels and plush versions of his mascots, which a spokesperson said embody the slogan "Future Soon". The campaign also credited a grassroots fan base dubbed "Ocean Current", a play on Shen's Chinese name, with producing its own stickers and banners.

Changhua County's contest has taken a more domestic turn. KMT contender Wei Ping-cheng is distributing tissues and UV arm sleeves manufactured at his family's factory, the packets adorned with a cartoon of him sketched by his daughter. Independent Chiu Chien-fu, meanwhile, hands out socks, which he says symbolise his resolve to go the extra mile alongside supporters.
In sweltering Tainan, the KMT's Hsieh Lung-chieh is circulating fans emblazoned with his policy pledges, whereas the DPP's Chen Ting-fei is selling teddy bears bearing the message "Tainan is home".

Ahead of Taiwan's local elections on November 28, candidates are relying on an established form of political marketing: campaign merchandise. Such items fulfil two functions simultaneously, generating revenue and reinforcing name recognition among an electorate exposed to countless competing messages.

In the capital, incumbent mayor Chiang Wan-an of the KMT has prioritised utility, offering tote bags, insulated bottles and phone wallets. His campaign has also turned to technology: an NFC keychain which, when tapped against a compatible phone, automatically directs users to the campaign's theme song.

His DPP opponent, Puma Shen, has opted for a more playful aesthetic, featuring plush mascots and embroidered patches that his team says encapsulate the slogan "Future Soon". Notably, the campaign has acknowledged a spontaneous supporter movement, nicknamed "Ocean Current" after a pun on Shen's Chinese name, which independently produces posters and badges.

In Changhua County, merchandise reflects a more personal, local character. KMT candidate Wei Ping-cheng distributes tissues produced at his family's factory, decorated with a cartoon drawn by his daughter, while independent Chiu Chien-fu offers socks as a metaphor for his commitment to going further with his supporters.

Regional conditions also shape these choices. In Tainan, renowned for its heat, KMT candidate Hsieh Lung-chieh distributes fans printed with his pledges, whereas the DPP's Chen Ting-fei sells teddy bears conveying the message "Tainan is home".

noteHi.exampleTr: नए शब्द दोहराने से याददाश्त मज़बूत होती है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ को और मज़बूत करना।
noteHi.usage: reinforce a message/idea आम प्रयोग है।

noteEs.exampleTr: Repetir palabras nuevas ayuda a reforzar la memoria.
noteEs.meaning: hacer algo más fuerte o firme.
noteEs.usage: Se usa reinforce a message / an idea.

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい単語を繰り返すと記憶が強化される。
noteJa.usage: reinforce a message / an idea の形。

relying.ex: Families relying on food banks need help.

renowned.ex: Galway is renowned for its festivals.

revenue.ex: Ticket sales are the theatre's main revenue.

example.en: Tourism generates most of the island's revenue.
example.zh: 觀光業為該島帶來大部分收入。

note.usage: 常見 generate/raise revenue；tax revenue；多用於公司或政府。

noteEn.meaning: money that a business or government receives.

noteHi.exampleTr: पर्यटन से द्वीप का अधिकांश राजस्व आता है।
noteHi.usage: generate revenue; tax revenue आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteEs.exampleTr: El turismo genera la mayor parte de los ingresos de la isla.
noteEs.meaning: ingresos de una empresa o gobierno.
noteEs.usage: Se usa generate revenue; tax revenue.

noteJa.exampleTr: 観光が島の収入の大半を生む。
noteJa.usage: generate revenue、tax revenue の形が多い。

noteKo.usage: generate revenue, tax revenue 형태가 흔하다.
